title: Probability Quiz
description: Practice working out simple chances, using the 0 to 1 scale, finding complements and multiplying chances for independent events.

questions.question: You flip a fair coin. What is the probability that it lands on heads?
questions.explanation: There are 2 equally likely outcomes, heads or tails, and 1 of them is heads. So the probability is 1/2.

questions.question: You roll a fair six-sided die. What is the probability of rolling a 5?
questions.explanation: There is 1 way to roll a 5 out of 6 possible outcomes, so the probability is 1/6.

questions.question: Which probability means an event is impossible?
questions.explanation: Probabilities go from 0 to 1. A probability of 0 means impossible and 1 means certain. A probability can never be negative.

questions.question: A bag has 4 red marbles and 6 blue marbles. You pick one without looking. What is the probability that it is red?
questions.explanation: There are 4 + 6 = 10 marbles and 4 are red, so the probability is 4/10, which simplifies to 2/5. Using 4/6 compares red to blue instead of red to the total.

questions.question: The chance of rain tomorrow is 30%. What is the chance that it does not rain?
questions.explanation: An event and its complement add up to 100%. So the chance of no rain is 100% − 30% = 70%.

questions.question: You roll a fair six-sided die. What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: Only 5 and 6 are greater than 4, so there are 2 ways out of 6. 2/6 simplifies to 1/3. Getting 1/2 means you counted 4 as well.

questions.question: You flip a coin and roll a six-sided die. What is the probability of getting heads and a 6?
questions.explanation: The coin and the die are independent, so multiply the chances. 1/2 × 1/6 = 1/12. Adding them gives 2/3, which is too big.

questions.question: You flip a fair coin 3 times. What is the probability of getting heads all 3 times?
questions.explanation: Each flip is independent with a 1/2 chance of heads. 1/2 × 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/8.

questions.question: A bag has 3 red and 2 green counters. You take one, put it back, then take another. What is the probability that both are green?
questions.explanation: The chance of green is 2/5 each time, and putting the counter back keeps the picks independent. 2/5 × 2/5 = 4/25.

questions.question: You roll two fair six-sided dice. What is the probability of getting at least one 6?
questions.explanation: Use the complement. The chance of no 6 on both dice is 5/6 × 5/6 = 25/36. So the chance of at least one 6 is 1 − 25/36 = 11/36.
